deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a printed page, p. 113 of a small German arithmetic textbook (the imprint on the next page reads Wolfenbüttel, Bindseil, 1790, with a reference to Hellwig 1777). It is bound into the Leiste bundle. The handwriting cut off in the left margin belongs to the facing manuscript page: Gauss's French note criticising Legendre (Mém. Paris 1785, p. 520) and his lemma on mμ+nν+pπ=0. The printed text itself is not by Gauss. Its subject is approximating a fraction by the convergents of its regular continued fraction.

(1) A proper fraction m/(am+n) is written as 1/(a+n/m). The text then gives the successive truncations 1/(a+1/p) and 1/(a+1/(p+1/t)), i.e. the continued fraction [0; a, p, t, ...].

(2) First convergent: 1/(a+1/p) = p/(pa+1), obtained by multiplying numerator and denominator by p.

(3) Second convergent: put α = 1/t. Then 1/(a+1/(p+α)) = (p+α)/(a(p+α)+1) = (tp+1)/(atp+t+a). The last step multiplies through by t.

(4) Example 345/437. Since 345 = 15·23 and 437 = 19·23, this equals 15/19 (the gcd 23 is my addition). Its continued fraction is 15/19 = [0;1,3,1,3], so a=1, p=3, t=1, u=3.
- 1/(1+1/3) = 3/4, and 15/19 − 3/4 = 3/76, so 3/4 is too small.
- (tp+1)/(atp+t+a) = 4/5, and 4/5 − 15/19 = 1/95, so 4/5 is too large.
This illustrates that the convergents alternate around the value.

(5) Third level: put α = 1/(t+1/u) = u/(ut+1). Then (p+α)/(a(p+α)+1) = (p(ut+1)+u)/(a(put+p+u)+ut+1). This is the full fraction in lowest terms, i.e. 345/437 with the common greatest divisor r (=23) removed.
- Check with a=1, p=3, t=1, u=3: numerator 3·4+3 = 15; denominator 9+3+3+3+1 = 19.

(6) Second example: diameter/circumference = 10^10/31415926536 ≈ 1/π = [0;3,7,15,1,292,...]. First convergent 1/(3+1/7) = 7/22. The page continues on p.114 with 106/331 and 113/355; 113/355 is below the given fraction by less than 3·10^-8 (actual ≈ 2.7·10^-8).
errors: The second-convergent denominator (shown on this page twice) prints as 'atp+t+n' in the image; it should be atp+t+a (the a=1 evaluation 4/5 is consistent with the correct form). Likely a typesetting slip, or the machine transcription silently corrected it.
Not an error, but implicit: the step 345/437 = 15/19 (common factor 23) is not shown on the page.
The phrase 'in den kleinsten Zahlen, die möglich sind' is correct, since continued-fraction convergents are automatically in lowest terms, but no justification is given.

results.what: Convergents of the regular continued fraction 1/(a+1/(p+1/(t+1/u))) expressed as explicit rational functions; approximating 345/437=15/19 by 3/4, 4/5, 15/19 with alternating errors 3/76 and 1/95
results.modern_name: Continued fraction convergents (best rational approximations), alternation property
results.usually_credited_to: Huygens, Wallis, Euler (17th–18th c.); textbook material by 1790

results.modern_name: Continued fraction expansion of π (Metius' approximation 355/113)
results.usually_credited_to: Zu Chongzhi / Adriaan Metius; continued fraction of π by Wallis/Huygens/Euler

deep.surprise_reason: This is a printed elementary textbook page (1790), not Gauss's own work. It presents standard continued-fraction convergents; the only Gauss trace is marginal handwriting spilling over from the facing manuscript page.

checkable.asserts: 113/355 is below the given ratio by about 2.7e-8 (< 3e-8)

transcription_corrections: In both occurrences on the page, the image shows the second-convergent denominator as 'atp+t+n' (the printed final letter looks like n, probably a misprint for a). The transcription gives 'atp+t+a', which is the mathematically correct form.

The marginal fragments on the left ('seulement', 'me An-1 qui', '1785. p. 520', 'cela ou de ne', 'tion en marge', 'p = mμ'+nν'...', 'C.') are bleed-through or overhang from the facing manuscript page (Gauss's note on Legendre and his lemma), not part of this page's content.
The page is printed type (Fraktur), not Gauss's manuscript; '113' is the printed page number.
